# Native project format regression fixtures

`v1-manifest.json` is a frozen, hand-authored version-1 document. Its raw RGBA8
payload is `v1-raster.hex`: three pixels per row, top row first. Distinct corners,
partial alpha and nonzero hidden RGB make orientation, premultiplication and
lossless-storage mistakes observable. The layer has a signed, nontrivial affine
transform and separate opacity. These fixtures contain no third-party assets.

`ProjectFileTests.cpp` wraps this fixture in a deterministic ZIP using an
independent, test-only minizip-ng/QBuffer adapter, not the production project
writer. ZIP timestamps are fixed. Store, Deflate and forced-ZIP64 variants are
generated in temporary directories; no binary fixtures or large raster files are
checked in. Malformed variants are generated by JSON mutation, duplicate ZIP
members, or byte-level corruption/truncation of the finished archive.

Coverage includes exact raster/rich-text/geometry round trips, optional defaults,
required features, invalid types/dimensions/IDs/paths, unknown metadata retention,
missing/duplicate/unexpected members, resource limits, CRC failures, truncation,
and cancellation/write failure preserving the previous destination. Resource
limit fixtures carry only tiny payloads, so the suite does not need gigabytes of
memory to reject oversized declarations.

The actual write-failure regression launches the test executable as a child with
`--write-failure PATH`. That child alone applies a 4096-byte soft `RLIMIT_FSIZE`
and ignores `SIGXFSZ`, producing an actual kernel write failure while saving a
256×256 fixed-seed, incompressible raster. The parent first verifies that the
same document saves normally, then verifies that its pre-existing destination,
temporary-directory contents and own resource limits remain unchanged. No
special device, disk filling, external target or global setting is involved.
